title: Knowledge Entry V1 (one stored revision of one knowledge entry)
$comment: DL-KB-02. This is the document src/design_lab/knowledge_library.py stores, one row per revision, and serves back verbatim. Every minimum field the taskpack names is present: internal id, type, title, summary, domain/task tags, body, applicability, counterexamples/limits, source, source version and observation time, license and citation scope, content digest, revision, and supersession. A field the caller did not supply is the literal string UNKNOWN -- the store writes that, it does not omit the key, so 'missing' is visible in the bytes a reader receives instead of being indistinguishable from 'empty'. A link in `source.origin` proves nothing: `source.verification` is always UNVERIFIED at this version, and the store refuses a caller that says otherwise. `content_sha256` covers the content-bearing fields only (see the module's _content_digest), so re-writing identical content as a new revision with a different recommendation is not a content change.

limits.description: Counterexamples and limits. UNKNOWN when the caller supplied none -- an empty string would read as 'no limits', which is a claim nobody made.

source.description: The field names are SourceRecord's own (design-lab/schemas/source-record.schema.json), so a reader who knows that record already knows this one. What is relaxed is only the strictness: SourceRecord forbids a missing license by schema, while a knowledge entry has to be able to say a field was not filled -- so the same keys carry UNKNOWN here. Nothing is upgraded to 'reviewed' by being written.

allOf.$comment: An unknown license may not be labelled reviewed, and a reviewed license may not be the literal UNKNOWN. The store enforces the same rule before validation; stating it in the contract keeps a second reader from having to trust the module.
